critique: The sharp primal–dual interval, finite-support endpoint representation, universal Bernstein-span identification criterion, and strict relative-interior width are actually proved for the note’s fixed-plate hierarchical class. The exact width result stops at the implicit identity 2d_m(epsilon): the shifted-Chebyshev construction supplies only an upper bound on d_m, with no matching lower formula or exact asymptotic. The CAD and boundary-atlas results establish generic quantifier-elimination termination but provide no executed endpoint certificate or explicit atlas, while whole-set coverage follows directly from count-law inversion. The São Paulo and Lee–Weidner connections remain motivational or restricted to the scalar-reference count-law transplant, so the results do not settle identification for either published model in its original form.
